title: Multi-agent-based Substation Information Management System

items.abstract: <jats:p>Multi-agent systems powered by large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in enterprise environments, where agents interact with tools, APIs, and each other through protocols such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP). A critical emerging threat is the compositional attack, where individually benign components produce malicious behavior through their interaction patterns. We propose a graph-topological feature framework that models agent–tool interactions as a heterogeneous directed graph and extracts an interpretable 58-dimensional feature vector from four complementary signal families: graph-structural analysis, semantic fidelity monitoring, persistent homology, and cycle-based interpretability certificates. The framework achieves AUC = 0.81 with a Random Forest classifier and provides cycle-level certificates that identify specific suspicious interaction paths an interpretability capability absent from end-to-end alternatives. While tuned graph neural networks achieve higher raw detection accuracy (GAT: 0.96, GCN: 0.91), they require labeled training data, GPU infrastructure, and produce no interpretable output. Our features are classifier-agnostic (AUC range = 0.066 across five classifiers including RF, GBT, SVM, LR, and MLP), generalize across domains (synthetic to-task transfer AUC = 0.90), and scale to 100-node systems with sub-400 ms end-to-end latency. Feature importance analysis reveals that graph-structural features provide the primary detection signal (72% of permutation importance), with persistent homology contributing statistically significant complementary information (𝑝 < 5 × 10−7). Detection quality exhibits a clear phase transition as attack coordination complexity increases from 𝑘 = 1 to 𝑘 = 8 components (AUC: 0.69 → 0.93).</jats:p>
